posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

In the late 9th century, Vikings have raided kingdom after kingdom and nearly conquered all of England. Wealthy monasteries and defenseless nuns were especially tempting targets and often suffered great losses. However, all of that stopped when Vikings were confronted by princess Aethelflaed, daughter of Alfred the Great.

Who was Lady of Mercia, and how did she shape the history of England by becoming Vikings' greatest nightmare? Watch our latest Nightshift video to find out! 🌚
Laughing gas can make you feel relaxed and euphoric in seconds. But it comes with serious risks as well. So, what exactly is laughing gas and why does it feel so good?

In the 17th century in Germany, one of Europe’s most terrifying witch hunts turned the town of Bamberg against itself. Tortures that occurred in the "Witch Factory" forced innocent people to name friends, neighbors and family members, creating a deadly chain reaction that eventually reached even the richest and most powerful, while those running the trials profited from the people they condemned.

competitors.bio: Discover the most incredible experiences from around the world 🌎✈️ Business: info@damiermedia.com

recentPosts.caption:
A Japanese-style hot spring experience… in Shanghai? ♨️🍵⁠
Step into a wooden tub, dress in traditional Japanese clothing if you wish, and enjoy tea in a cozy setting inspired by a peaceful onsen.⁠
⁠
@dama.dessert showed us Huixi Mountain Culture Hall, where the relaxing atmosphere, tea, and traditional sweets turn a simple café visit into a truly unique experience.⁠
⁠
Would you try the throne experience?

One of Iceland’s most unique stargazing spots is in the remote village of Raufarhöfn.⁠
⁠
Arctic Henge is a huge stone structure inspired by Norse mythology and built to frame the sky and create a striking setting for watching the stars.⁠
⁠
Located far from Iceland’s busiest tourist routes, it offers dark skies and, when conditions are right, a chance to see the Northern Lights overhead.⁠
⁠
By: @niko.laurila @wu_yee7

Imagine wandering through a Spanish village where the cliffs become part of the architecture.⁠
Setenil de las Bodegas in Andalusia is famous for its homes, restaurants, and narrow streets tucked beneath enormous rock overhangs. ⁠
⁠
The unusual layout developed over centuries, with the rock providing natural shelter from the region’s hot summers and cooler weather.⁠
A place that proves some of Spain’s most fascinating sights aren’t always the most famous ones. ⁠
🎥: @katiushaaaaa

Franklin Park Zoo is glowing after dark.⁠
⁠
After sunset, the zoo transforms with colorful illuminated displays, bringing the grounds and its animal-themed installations to life in a completely different way.⁠
⁠
It’s a fun way to experience one of Boston’s favorite attractions after sunset. ⁠
⁠
By: @zoonewengland

Once a year, Nara’s Great Buddha gets a very serious spring cleaning. 🧹🇯🇵⁠
Every August 7, Todaiji Temple holds Ominugui, a traditional ceremony dedicated to removing a year’s worth of dust and preparing the statue for Obon.⁠
⁠
Around 120 monks and helpers take part, using long brooms and dusters to clean the enormous Buddha, which stands roughly 15 meters tall. Some are even raised by gondola to reach the higher sections. 👀⁠
🎥: @hiroko_japan.travel

This unique staircase in London took 10,000 hours to create.⁠
⁠
Known as StairStalk, the sculptural staircase runs through three levels of HIDE restaurant in Mayfair.⁠
⁠
The staircase was hand-carved before being brought to London and installed at @hide_restaurant.⁠
⁠
By: @kam_visions⁠

No menu, no cocktail descriptions, and no idea what you’re ordering. 😂🍸⁠
At Anonymous Shrinks Office in Prague, you choose your drink from a series of photos and leave the rest to the bartenders.⁠
⁠
Your cocktail remains a mystery until it arrives, making the experience part of the fun.⁠
Would you trust the photo and order one? 👀⁠
⁠
⁠
🎥: @brettandtash

This tree looks like it was painted.⁠
⁠
The rainbow eucalyptus is known for its striking multicolored bark, which naturally changes shades as different layers are shed throughout the year.⁠
⁠
Greens, blues, purples, oranges, and reds can appear across the trunk, creating the look of a tree covered in brushstrokes.⁠
⁠
By: @the_wandering2 ⁠

Ever stayed inside a giant wine barrel? 🍷🏡⁠
@pacheca.group , guests can spend the night in beautifully converted wine barrels surrounded by the region’s vineyards.⁠
⁠
The stay comes with its own private pool, breakfast, and even peacocks wandering through the property making it a pretty unforgettable romantic escape. 🦚⁠
⁠
🎥: @chella.travels

Kelimutu is home to three volcanic crater lakes on the island of Flores, and their colors can shift over time as volcanic gases and minerals react with the water.⁠
⁠
One lake might appear blue or green, while another can turn red, brown, white, or even black.⁠
⁠
There’s no set schedule for the changes, so the lakes you see today may not look the same on your next visit!⁠
⁠
By: @by_ewold @calicarlo_⁠

A hidden gem, to say the least. 🏔️🇳🇵⁠
@duluwa_bhai gives us a glimpse of Lomanthang, a remote Himalayan town where dramatic landscapes, ancient traditions, and centuries-old culture come together.⁠
⁠
Far from the usual tourist trails, it’s the kind of place that feels like stepping into another world.⁠
Would you visit?

Some restaurants are worth planning an entire trip around.⁠
⁠
From unforgettable locations to incredible food and one-of-a-kind dining experiences, these are the kind of places that make the journey part of the experience.⁠
⁠
Which one would you travel for?⁠
⁠
By: @dinnerinthesky_official @underlindesnes @ristorantegrottapalazzese @travelsters_at @arcticsnowhotel @iristherestaurant @conrad_maldives

Lions are one of nature's most incredible creatures—but they need our help. By working together, we can create a better future for these remarkable big cats. Thats why PATH has teamed up with @natgeosociety and #NatGeoLION on a collab supporting Lion populations. 

Every PATH bottle purchase helps support the U.S. based global nonprofit National Geographic Society, which works to protect and illuminate our world through exploration, research and education. To learn more, visit https://on.natgeo.

Whorls, hexagons, and half-moon patterns can be found throughout nature, formed by natural processes such as wind and crashing waves. After spending time along the seashore, photographer and conservationist Jon McCormack discovered that our planet's familiar shapes and designs have guided his work for years. To celebrate this, he set out on a journey to capture nature's intriguing forms at every scale.

See more from his award-winning book and learn about nature's patterns at the link in bio.

Journalist and activist Gloria Steinem has passed away at the age of 92. Known informally as the “World’s Most Famous Feminist,” Steinem spent a lifetime fighting for women's rights. After graduating from college in 1956, Steinem began her journalism career in New York, writing pieces on contraception, exploitation, and other feminist issues. In the decades that followed, she devoted her time to spreading the word about why women's lives were as important as men's.

Retiring at 100 years old? Not a chance! Here’s a sneak peek of Sir David Attenborough working on the narration for the upcoming BLUE PLANET III.

#DavidAttenborough100 #DavidAttenborough #BluePlanetIII

This is what safety in numbers looks like 🐟 🐟 🐟
 
Faced with hungry predators, thousands of fish gather into one enormous, constantly moving bait ball. The sheer numbers make it difficult for a hunter to focus on just one. Sticking together is the best defence for these fish. 
 
Revisit 25 years of extraordinary ocean stories from Blue Planet with us. Find out where to watch the full series via the link in our bio 🔗
 
#BluePlanet #25Anniversary #MarineAnimals #Underwater

The ocean floor is full of surprises 👀
 
Hidden in plain sight on the seafloor, angel sharks are built for ambush. They can stay buried in the sand for days before lunging at passing prey, but even perfect camouflage doesn’t guarantee a successful strike. 
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

The solar system isn’t for the faint-hearted 🌌 🪐

From the scorching surface of Venus to the volcanic chaos of Io, our solar system is home to some truly hostile worlds. 

Discover which could be the scariest place of all via the link in bio.

#SolarSystem #Planets #Venus #Jupiter

Bet you didn’t see that coming 👀
 
Buried beneath the sand, angel sharks can lie perfectly camouflaged and wait for days for prey to swim by. Once a fish gets close enough, they burst from the seabed to strike. But does this technique always work?
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

Four billion years of evolution, brought to life on T-shirts. 🧬 🦠

Inspired by the extraordinary stories and iconic animals featured in Evolution, explore the collection and shop with Teemill via the link in our bio.
 
#Evolution #Merch #Design #Tshirt

Finding your feet 👣

Over 500 million years ago, flecks of food drifting on ocean currents were eaten by small animals on the seabed, but the flow would often change. To reach them, some tried a pioneering action: they would move. These are thought to be some of the first animal tracks on Earth.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Who knew the ocean has a public transport system 🦀
 
Columbus crabs aren’t built for long-distance swimming, so this little crab takes a shortcut through the open ocean. By hitchhiking a ride on a turtle, he find transport, a new home and some unexpected company.
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

More than meets the eye 👀

Ancient ancestors of the dolphin hid from the sun’s UV rays using two light-detecting spots. Fascinatingly, some inherited mutations that allowed them to perceive light and shade together, so they could visualise their environment - essentially becoming the first proper eyes.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

From fantasy to reality 🦇

Evolution presenter @chrisgpackham2 reveals how coming face-to-face with some extraordinary bats fulfilled a childhood dream.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Turns out the forest has a group chat 📞
 
Treehoppers might be tiny, but they’ve got plenty to say! They communicate through vibrations sent along the plants they live on, most of which are too quiet for us to hear. But when danger appears, sending the right signal can make all the difference.
